verdict.rationale: Microsoft Graph's documented mail API covers every verb the story needs: read, filter/search, categorize, flag, inbox rules, draft and send. So any agent able to make authenticated HTTP calls can run the full loop programmatically. However, the evidence shows no first-party agent connector (MCP server, Claude/ChatGPT integration), so the user or a developer must wire up the connection themselves. Agent-oriented doc probes (llms.txt, markdown docs, OpenAPI) all returned 404. missing for 10: an official agent-facing connector or MCP server for Claude/ChatGPT, machine-readable agent docs (llms.txt/OpenAPI), and independent hands-on corroboration of an agent running read-triage-draft-send end to end.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, an external agent — Claude, ChatGPT, or my own — can read, triage, draft, and send my email end to end through a documented connection
